raspi-scripte:1.1:
Version 1.1 – Changes since 1.0.30

1. Before Allsky starts, a Witty RTC showing year 2000 is initialised to 1 January 2026, 00:00:00 and written back. Other years are retained. Time synchronisation is still verified and time-zone/fixed-offset settings are preserved. This fallback is not the current time.
2. Both manual GPS time buttons accept valid GPS time with Allsky installed. Witty remains the automatic time source before Allsky starts. Existing write/read-back checks remain.
3. Additional settings: current measurement sits between voltage and temperature; power-on at supply is clearly labelled before Witty Reset; Reset is at the end before Raspberry restart. Hot standby is removed. Energy priority is renamed Preferred power input.
4. UTC selector: larger text, alternating subtle backgrounds and arrows on +01:00, +02:00 and +10:00. Time-zone guidance precedes the selector and the active mode is green.
5. On desktop, date/time inputs sit directly beside their respective Set buttons.
6. GPS: installed variant is green above its button; the status light still shows activity. Duplicate text/divider removed; GPS time is hidden without valid time data.
7. Firmware changes are acknowledged before the subsequent quick status refresh, which does not query GPS.
8. Script directories and metadata are read in one Witty transaction, stopping/restarting wp5d only once. Systemd start limits are unchanged.

The reported spontaneous Raspberry outages were not conclusively diagnosed. Logs showed repeated undervoltage and an abrupt end without a corresponding Witty shutdown entry. This release was not presented as a confirmed outage fix.

raspi-scripte:1.1.4.1:
Version 1.1.4.1 – Full rollback to version 1.1 functionality

Base installation, manufacturer installation, Raspberry services, WURB/WIRC/Allsky setup, homepage and Windows use the original 1.1 functional files from 27 October 2026. Later changes, including diagnostic additions, are excluded. The common release identifier is 1.1.4.1.
The full Windows package now contains the same content/add-on as separate downloads, replacing its stale embedded 1.0.30 package with the common 1.1 base. All installation entry points therefore use the same Raspberry code.
The Windows executable and updater match the original. Only display/update version and date fields in the main DLL were changed; startup, SSH, installation, networking, shutdown and activation identity were retained. Full program updates include matching content.
The existing Pi 5 Ethernet enablement after 30 seconds remains and is installed for WURB after WURB/WIRC packages. It contains no shutdown command; a missing helper was not established as the cause of the early installation failure.
Validation at that release covered original-code and Windows-method comparisons, matching embedded packages, Bash/Python syntax, ZIP/authenticated-encryption integrity, checksums and extraction of the original updater. No physical Raspberry installation/boot or native WPF test was performed. This was a rollback, not a proven hardware fix.

raspi-scripte:1.1.4.2:
Version 1.1.4.2 – Verified restart after base installation

1. WURB, WIRC and Allsky base installation finishes through witty-reboot rather than direct systemctl reboot. Before completion, the manufacturer restart service, enablement and reboot.target integration are checked.
2. A missing helper or failed preparation stops with a clear error; there is no unchecked fallback restart. Request failures are reported explicitly.
3. Separate downloads, Windows content and both bundled add-ons contain the same 1.1.4.2 add-on. Windows binaries/background polling remain unchanged; content version is updated.
Validation at that release covered syntax of 44 shell files, simulated successful restart, missing helper, failed preparation/request, archive integrity, encryption and identical packages.
The reported abort after step=checks occurred before the installation summary/final restart and was not conclusively diagnosed. No physical Pi/Witty boot or native WPF test was performed; this was not a confirmed fix for that abort.

raspi-scripte:1.1.4.3:
Version 1.1.4.3 – Restore the Witty service after clock actions and retain the console

1. Clock helpers/backend restore a previously running manufacturer service after errors, cancellation and external timeout. Restoration is armed before stopping and the result is verified. Failed restart is not treated as success.
2. GPS is queried/validated while the service runs. Manufacturer installation checks the time zone before the short stopped phase and reads back afterwards. Pi 5 boot sync uses the existing reader for a valid Witty RTC without stopping the service or rewriting the RTC; year-2000 fallback is retained.
3. Base installation copies the same clock helper as updates. Both verify/start the manufacturer service before success. The fix retains manufacturer package 5.3.1 and existing Witty settings.
4. The shared restart helper no longer performs full RTC/GPS synchronisation immediately before restart. Temporary package time is rolled back on Linux only, followed by service checks, sync and normal systemd restart without forced reset. Windows/GPS restart use the same helper; failed preparation has no fallback restart.
5. Windows collapses the SSH console after updates but retains history, prompt and input. Reconnection does not automatically clear history; manual clearing remains available.
6. Program/content are version 1.1.4.3; separate downloads and both embedded add-ons use identical corrected installation code.
Validation at that release included 23 cancellation/timing cases, TERM handling, service restoration, GPS ordering, boot sync without service stop, restart ordering/failure, Bash/Python syntax, Windows build, terminal/connection protocol checks and archive/encryption/package equality. No physical Pi/Witty or native WPF test; the software fault was reproduced/fixed, but its role in the reported startup outage was not proven.

raspi-scripte:1.2:
Version 1.2 – Direct script editing, mobile controls and consistent navigation

Changes since 1.1.4.3:
1. Update output contains only changes after the installed version/build, progress, warnings, errors and outcome. Historical setup text/release filenames are omitted; WITTY_UPDATE_VERBOSE=1 enables detailed diagnostics.
2. Mobile WURB position polling and delayed defaults preserve edits. Status refresh preserves scroll position during entry, intentional scrolling remains possible, and input sizing avoids iPhone focus zoom.
3. Manual positions are saved/read back and compared; decimal commas and leading/trailing N/S/E/W are accepted. Errors and failed inputs remain visible. Source changes and saves are processed in order.
4. GPS setup preserves manual sources/coordinates in current, startup and user profiles. WURB's separate startup profile selection remains.
5. Hidden/uninstalled services no longer leave a stray red navigation light. Accepted formats is below Save.
6. Witty mobile fields have light backgrounds, black text, clearer borders and readable placeholders/disabled values. Red/green status colours remain; desktop is unaffected.
7. Add-on pages share navigation dimensions, 36-pixel buttons, typography/spacing and a white active-page marker. On original WURB/WIRC/Allsky pages only supplementary navigation is aligned.
8. Recording folder icons/names toggle folders and subfolders with each click, matching the existing button. Checkboxes/ZIP download remain independent.
9. The intermediate Current script/Copy to editor area is removed. Current/saved scripts load directly into the sole editor, including the active script from the file list; mobile editor expands. Loading does not change the running schedule.
10. Imports are not silently truncated to 4,000 bytes. Size violations are displayed and prevent upload. Filename, BEGIN/END, line numbers, preview and validation refresh on load. German/English guides updated.
11. Windows homepage buttons are renamed/aligned by application and use the connected Pi on Witty 8081, WURB 8080 and WIRC 8082.
12. Windows, content and add-on use 1.2 with identical base/separate/bundled packages. Service restoration and console retention from 1.1.4.3 remain.
Validation at that release covered 64 targeted Python/JavaScript cases, including 23 clock/service cases, plus rebuilt program/updater and archive/encryption/version/package checks. No physical Pi/Witty, real phone-keyboard or native Windows/browser layout test was performed; compilation alone does not prove target layout.

raspi-scripte:1.2.0:
Version 1.2.0 – PC time before installation and updates

Only when the Raspberry system clock differs from the PC by more than 48 hours does Windows automatically apply current PC time before the first download check. This also applies with Allsky installed, direct Internet access and Windows-assisted download. The system time is read back before download/update continues; the previous prompt is removed. Neither RTC nor the time zone is written. HTTPS certificate verification stays enabled.
Validation at that release covered the Windows cross-build and automated clock/preflight tests. No physical Raspberry/Witty or native WPF test was performed.

raspi-scripte:1.3.9:
Version 1.3.9 – 7 November 2026

- Live Video Image: execute popup code; closing, Escape and connection loss end the preview. Discard late frames after closing.
- Resume only a previously running Allsky service. Report stop/restart failures and retain pending recovery. Exclude concurrent configuration/storage operations during preview.
- Read valid archive versions and aliases from the source catalog. Accept the November archive while still rejecting mismatched Git revisions, allowing the existing automatic reboot path after successful installation.
- Apply the same Witty camera, package/Python and Trixie preparation to archive and direct upstream installations. Current upstream core e9309b09 matches the November archive core. Archived support modules remain pinned; direct installation uses upstream sources.
- Use dated allsky-v2026.11.03-e9309b09 download paths and remove duplicate archive filenames.
- Complete English setup labels, including storage space, sun angle and popup. Hide explanatory copy on phones while retaining status and controls. Default the Allsky mobile homepage to Australian English when no preference exists, preserving an explicit language choice.
- Label the November snapshot Allsky · Archive 3 November 2026 instead of showing the internal October upstream version as its visible name.
- Fit long ALLSKY_Setup buttons on phones and default to English when language preference is cleared.

Validation: original October/November sources with and without GS, helper/file tests and browser tests with simulated API/video data. Real camera preview and a complete 1.3.9 installation/reboot on the Raspberry remain untested. Bash syntax validation unavailable on this Windows test host.
Windows content package 1.3.9 includes the identical Witty package. The Windows executable remains the unchanged 1.3.8 binary; no new EXE build.

raspi-scripte:1.4:
Version 1.4 – 7 November 2026

- Refresh and verify the installed Allsky camera helper; invoke the current packaged patch directly. Support both camera database filenames without requiring an OV5647 sensor entry.
- Consume completed installation timezone snapshots. Historical snapshots cannot override the selected fixed UTC offset at startup.
- Apply the selected fixed offset unchanged, without deriving another offset from a region's daylight-saving rules. Select the actual active offset in the webpage and avoid stale custom-zone cache data.
- Windows, content and both embedded add-on copies share release 1.4. Retain all 1.3.9 changes.
- Software regression checks and Windows build/tests; no physical installation test on the affected Raspberry Pi.

witty-addon:1.4.1:
Version 1.4.1 – 9 November 2026

- Store the regional time zone separately from a fixed UTC offset. Australia/Sydney applies daylight saving without GPS.
- Preserve Allsky's saved fixed offset when WURB/WIRC return to regional automatic time.
- Reload time rules in running WURB/WIRC processes and invalidate WURB solar caches on zone/day changes. Resolve the solar calculation date at call time.
- Apply fresh progressing GPS fixes in an independent background service, including late receiver attachment or late reception. GPS acquisition no longer holds the Witty command lock.
- Share short-lived status snapshots across clients and avoid queueing background reads ahead of user actions. Bound HTTP requests.
- Refresh Witty RTC at daylight-saving transitions from Linux time without requiring GPS.
- Add a black-bordered Windows time panel with PC UTC sync and fixed/automatic time-zone dialogs; detect and display the PC time zone and verify applied settings.
- Repair both Witty lock-file permissions during install, Add-on update and manufacturer installation. Reconnect the terminal after group changes.
- Retain the published 1.4 Allsky/archive/UTC corrections.

Validation includes a Windows build, language syntax checks and focused software regression tests. Both physical Raspberry Pi/GPS installations remain untested.

- Updated Windows and homepage user guides and release notes in German and Australian English, covering time modes, UTC selection, GPS clock actions, Allsky live view and updates.

raspi-scripte:1.4.1:
Version 1.4.1 – 9 November 2026

- Store the regional time zone separately from a fixed UTC offset. Australia/Sydney applies daylight saving without GPS.
- Preserve Allsky's saved fixed offset when WURB/WIRC return to regional automatic time.
- Reload time rules in running WURB/WIRC processes and invalidate WURB solar caches on zone/day changes. Resolve the solar calculation date at call time.
- Apply fresh progressing GPS fixes in an independent background service, including late receiver attachment or late reception. GPS acquisition no longer holds the Witty command lock.
- Share short-lived status snapshots across clients and avoid queueing background reads ahead of user actions. Bound HTTP requests.
- Refresh Witty RTC at daylight-saving transitions from Linux time without requiring GPS.
- Add a black-bordered Windows time panel with PC UTC sync and fixed/automatic time-zone dialogs; detect and display the PC time zone and verify applied settings.
- Repair both Witty lock-file permissions during install, Add-on update and manufacturer installation. Reconnect the terminal after group changes.
- Retain the published 1.4 Allsky/archive/UTC corrections.

Validation includes a Windows build, language syntax checks and focused software regression tests. Both physical Raspberry Pi/GPS installations remain untested.

- Live Video Image: execute popup code; closing, Escape and connection loss end the preview. Discard late frames after closing.

- Fit long ALLSKY_Setup buttons on phones and default to English when language preference is cleared.

Validation: original October/November sources with and without GS, helper/file tests and browser tests with simulated API/video data. Real camera preview and a complete 1.3.9 installation/reboot on the Raspberry remain untested. Bash syntax validation unavailable on this Windows test host.

witty:1.2.0:
Version 1.2.0 – PC time before installation and updates

Only when the Raspberry system clock differs from the PC by more than 48 hours does Windows automatically apply current PC time before the first download check. This also applies with Allsky installed, direct Internet access and Windows-assisted download. The system time is read back before download/update continues; the previous prompt is removed. Neither RTC nor the time zone is written. HTTPS certificate verification stays enabled.
Validation at that release covered the Windows cross-build and automated clock/preflight tests. No physical Raspberry/Witty or native WPF test was performed.
raspi-scripte:1.2.0.1:
Version 1.2.0.1 – Homepage, startup status and script activation

1. Automatic power-on and preferred power input lead Additional settings before input voltage. Internal Pi RTC precedes RPI - reboot and RPI - shut down.
2. Date/time inputs align vertically with actions beside them; redundant manual labels removed. GPS buttons are renamed GPS => system time + Witty Pi RTC and GPS => Witty Pi RTC without changing their actions. Mobile rows wrap and GPS buttons stack.
3. Windows homepage buttons align beside the matching software rows.
4. Original WURB Accepted formats guidance sits below Save on desktop/mobile, preserving original text/visibility.
5. GPS time-zone database loads on demand. Quick status waits up to two seconds for the backend lock, retries initial failures, and shows current-data/time labels only after success.
6. Activate is hidden after END using Witty RTC, even while the page stays open. Backend preflight rejects expired known sources. Editing/deleting remain possible; dates are not changed automatically.
7. Activation gives immediate elapsed-time feedback. Terminal firmware errors do not cause minutes of repeated activation/alarm reset. Activation finished, but… is a failure; only a confirming manufacturer reply establishes success.
8. Automatic PC time correction before base installation/Witty update remains limited to differences exceeding 48 hours.
Validation at that release covered Windows cross-build and targeted Python/JavaScript tests. No physical Raspberry/Witty or native WPF test was performed.
